Visual Look Up in Photos vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Visual Look Up in system Photos covers storefront language. On-device identification and Connect actually separate photo-lookup behavior from product-page copy:

  • Visual Look Up in Photos, Camera, and Safari — long-press an image or tap the info (i) button to surface identification results for plants, pets, landmarks, art, food, books, and symbols. Labeled 视觉查找 in zh-Hans system UI. Does not generate Chinese App Store listing text.
  • Look Up on selected photo — the buyer-visible outcome when Visual Look Up recognizes a subject: species name, breed info, landmark details, artwork attribution, nutrition facts, or book metadata. Your listing may show before/after lookup sheets on gallery frames; building identification backends is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Category-specific identification apps — plant encyclopedias, pet breed guides, travel landmark companions, art museum apps, food scanners, and book ISBN lookup tools that market "works with Visual Look Up" or "identify from any photo" on the product page. Listing copy describes the benefit; Vision or Core ML code lives in the binary.

  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Visual Look Up support in iOS or iPadOS.

Visual Look Up working on buyer devices and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.
